title: Danger, Dr. Danfield
paragraphs: Crime drama about criminal psychologist Dr. Daniel Danfield, who analyzes criminals and reconstructs cases for his secretary Rusty Fairfax while assisting law enforcement investigations.
Crime/detective drama built around criminal psychologist Dr. Daniel Danfield dictating solved cases to secretary Rusty Fairfax.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: 26-program surviving transcription sequence (August 18, 1946 to February 9, 1947) on [[org|org.danfield.71a100e9e828f785|American Broadcasting Company]] and Documented ABC network airing span (August 18, 1946 to April 13, 1947) on [[org|org.danfield.71a100e9e828f785|American Broadcasting Company]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Michael Dunn (performer), Ralph Wilkinson (writer), Wally Ramsey (producer), Joanne Johnson (performer), and Joanne Jackson (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to criminal psychology and behavioral inference, police consultation and criminal investigation, murder and suspicious death, apparently supernatural or uncanny clues, deception, fraud and hidden motives, and insurance, money and financial crime.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Criminal psychologist as radio detective, Teleways transcription and syndication model, ABC network and Knox sponsorship, and Surviving package versus longer network chronology.
